en.title: Minimum Machines for Closed-Interval Tasks
en.description:
Each task occupies one machine during [start,end], endpoints included, and each machine runs at most one task at any moment. Find the minimum number of machines. Original example 2 contains an invalid task with start>end and its explanation re-pairs the values, so this corrupted example is not used.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of start end; full original bounds 1≤n≤200000, 1≤start≤end≤1000000000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; 4; 2. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Add one at each task's start and subtract one at the moment right after its end, then scan in time order for the maximum number of tasks running at once.
